implementation_notes: The presentation model is a class implementing INotifyPropertyChanged: every bindable field has a property whose setter raises PropertyChanged, and derived display state (ComposerEnabled) is a read-only property; commands are ICommand properties whose CanExecute reads the model. XAML binds controls to the model (DataContext) and the framework performs the synchronization. The INotifyPropertyChanged documentation itself shows the CallerMemberName attribute as the way to raise the event without string literals.
pitfalls: A missing, misspelled or wrong property name in PropertyChanged breaks exactly one binding with no error; CallerMemberName or nameof keeps the name correct.
Raising PropertyChanged from a background thread updates bound controls on that thread, which WPF refuses; marshal to the UI thread or use the framework dispatcher.
Setters that raise without comparing to the old value create feedback loops between two mutually bound properties, so every setter must test for a real change.

variants.name: CommunityToolkit.Mvvm source-generated observable model
variants.implementation_notes: The MVVM Toolkit generates the notification plumbing: annotate a field in a partial class deriving from ObservableObject with [ObservableProperty] and the generator emits a property whose setter calls SetProperty (with the On<Name>Changing/On<Name>Changed partial hooks); [NotifyPropertyChangedFor] raises dependent property notifications, [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor] re-evaluates an IRelayCommand's CanExecute, and ObservableValidator forwards data-annotation validation. The model stays a plain testable object; the classic hand-written INotifyPropertyChanged form remains justified when the package or generators are unavailable or a property needs custom semantics.
pitfalls: The annotated field must live in a partial class with the INotifyPropertyChanged infrastructure; nested types must all be partial or the generator fails.

Only attributes deriving from ValidationAttribute are forwarded from the field to the generated property, so other field attributes (serialization, for example) must be written with an explicit [property: ...] target.
Dependent notifications are opt-in: forgetting [NotifyPropertyChangedFor] leaves computed properties such as ComposerEnabled stale even though the generator updated the field.
